name: CUPID-Mo neutrinoless double-beta decay search with Li2(100)MoO4 scintillating bolometers and Ge light detectors at 20.7 mK
plain_name: Search for neutrinoless double-beta decay with lithium molybdate crystals read out by heat and light at 20 mK
description: Underground rare-event search: 20 enriched Li2100MoO4 crystals (~44 mm diameter, ~45 mm high, 4.158 kg total) each paired with a Ge-wafer light detector and NTD Ge thermistors are suspended in towers inside the EDELWEISS-III dilution refrigerator and operated at 20.7 mK, recording heat and scintillation signals for particle identification.
keywords: Search for neutrinoless double-beta decay with lithium molybdate crystals read out by heat and light at 20 mK

sources.citation: The CUPID-Mo experiment for neutrinoless double-beta decay: performance and prospects (Armengaud et al., arXiv:1909.02994)

reported_equipment: EDELWEISS-III dilution refrigerator (reversed geometry) at LSM

requirements.rationale: Detectors were operated at a stable 20.7 mK.
The cryostat must reach the 20.7 mK working temperature.
Each crystal is ~44 mm in diameter.
NTD thermistors and heaters on every crystal and light detector must be wired out.
The full array of 20 crystals has 4.158 kg to be cooled.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
